chunks: I said: Some of your freed slaves have narrated from your forefathers (peace be upon them) that every endowment (waqf) for a known time period is obligatory upon the inheritors, and every endowment for an unknown time period is ignorance, unknown, invalid, and returned to the inheritors. And you are more knowing of the speech of your forefathers. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is with me, as such.'

key_terms.وَقْفٍ: Endowment (waqf), a form of charitable dedication of property

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an endowment with an unknown duration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms the precedent set by his forefathers, establishing a clear jurisprudential distinction between fixed-term endowments, which remain binding on heirs, and indefinite ones, which are deemed invalid due to uncertainty (gharar). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on clarity in legal conditions to prevent disputes over inheritance and property rights. The Imam's response ('It is so with me') validates this as an established sunnah rather than a novel interpretation.
